guide.summary: The Alhambra, the cathedral quarter, Sacromonte caves and Albaicín flamenco, with restaurants, cafés, a bakery and drinks terraces checked against their own websites.
guide.tip: Buy Alhambra tickets in advance and collect them at least an hour before the Nasrid Palaces time printed on your ticket, because entry is only allowed at that time.

toolkit.label: Closing days
toolkit.copy: Parque de las Ciencias and the Centro Federico García Lorca close on Mondays, and Mirador de Morayma and Carmen de San Miguel close on both Sundays and Mondays. Chikito closes on Wednesdays.

toolkit.label: Tickets and booking
toolkit.copy: The Alhambra limits advance sales to 10 tickets per person and card per month, and you must enter the Nasrid Palaces at the time on your ticket. Fundación Rodríguez-Acosta tickets are also for a set time and are not valid once that time has passed.

toolkit.label: Walk-in policies
toolkit.copy: Hammam Al Ándalus requires advance booking, recommends 2 to 3 days' notice, and charges in full for changes made less than 48 hours ahead. El Huerto de Juan Ranas takes reservations for its terrace online only.

toolkit.label: Rules
toolkit.copy: At Fundación Rodríguez-Acosta you leave backpacks and large bags at reception, and interior photography is not allowed. Hammam Al Ándalus requires a swimsuit, and at the Alhambra the person who booked collects machine tickets with their ID and the card used to pay.

guide.dek: Fix your Alhambra slot first, then plan the cathedral quarter and the Albaicín around the Monday and Sunday closures.
intro: The Alhambra shapes most visits to Granada, and its own site sets out the rules. In the winter period, from 15 October to 31 March, daytime visits run every day from 08:30 to 18:00, and evening visits run on Friday and Saturday from 20:00 to 21:30. You must enter the Nasrid Palaces at the time printed on your ticket, and the Patronato recommends buying early because demand is high. Children under 12 go free, but their tickets must be bought at the same time as everyone else's. The site closes only on 25 December and 1 January.

In the centre, the Cathedral and the Capilla Real stand side by side, and both sites ask you to confirm hours before you go. The Capilla Real opens daily except Good Friday, 25 December and 1 January. On the same street, the Palacio de la Madraza is open Monday to Friday from 09:00 to 21:00, and its exhibition on Arab and Islamic scientific heritage, La casa de la ciencia, runs until 22 December 2026. Near the Alhambra, Fundación Rodríguez-Acosta sells timed tickets, asks you to leave large bags at reception and does not allow photography indoors.

In Sacromonte, the Museo Cuevas del Sacromonte keeps winter hours from 26 October, opening every day from 10:00 to 18:00, with general entry at 6 euros. Hammam Al Ándalus on Calle Santa Ana requires advance booking and a swimsuit, and its sessions last 90 minutes including massage time. For flamenco, Jardines de Zoraya in the Albaicín stages shows at 18:00, 20:00 and 22:30, and children under seven go free. Cueva de la Rocío on Camino del Sacromonte offers shows with a drink or with dinner. If you are travelling with children, Parque de las Ciencias is closed on Mondays.

Plan your meals around closing days. Carmen de San Miguel and Mirador de Morayma close on Sundays and Mondays, Chikito closes on Wednesdays, and Damasqueros serves only lunch on Sundays and closes on Mondays. Restaurante El Agua in the Albaicín serves lunch and dinner every day, and Los Manueles on Reyes Católicos keeps its kitchen open from noon to midnight. For mornings, Café Futbol opens at 08:00, Despiertoo has cafés on Calle Jáudenes and Gran Vía, and Malamiga bakes sourdough and croissants. B-Heaven, the rooftop at Barceló Carmen, serves cocktails from 15:00 to 21:00.
summaryCards: Book a timed Alhambra ticket, then spend a second day on the Cathedral, the Capilla Real and the Palacio de la Madraza on Calle Oficios.
Start with coffee at Despiertoo or a croissant at Malamiga, then walk up to the Museo Cuevas del Sacromonte, which opens at 10:00.
Check closing days: Parque de las Ciencias closes on Mondays, and Carmen de San Miguel and Mirador de Morayma close on Sundays and Mondays.

limitations: Website review, not a visit or telephone confirmation. Advertised opening, booking and exhibition details do not guarantee availability. Several confirmed places published only partial information: the Catedral, Capilla Real and Basílica de San Juan de Dios showed only special or holiday hours, Monasterio de la Cartuja, Hammam Al Ándalus and Fundación Rodríguez-Acosta published no weekly hours, and Café Futbol, Malamiga, Bohemia Jazz Café, El Huerto de Juan Ranas and Cueva de la Rocío showed no 2026-dated content beyond published hours or bookings. The Museo Cuevas del Sacromonte gives its location only as Barranco de los Negros, and its www host had a certificate error, so the apex domain was read. The Centro Federico García Lorca homepage carries an unrelated gambling-app link, which suggests third-party spam on the site. Sites that could not be read include the Museo de Bellas Artes (Junta de Andalucía), Parador de Granada, Hotel Alhambra Palace, Casa Ysla, La Fábula, Puesto 43, Ruta del Azafrán and the Ayuntamiento de Granada monuments pages. The Generalife gardens exhibition at the Palacio de Carlos V ended on 24 May 2026.
